newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Consitutional Court member approved.
newsitem.headline: Russian Consitutional Court member approved.

text.p: Russia's upper house of parliament, the Federation Council, on Wednesday approved the appointment of a new Constitutional Court judge, 42-year-old Lyudmila Zharkova, by an overwhelming majority.

Zharkova, nominated by President Boris Yeltsin, becomes the third woman on the 19-member court, which in recent years has been seen as generally supportive of the Kremlin in disputes with the opposition-dominated lower house of parliament, the Duma.

An ethnic Finnish lawyer from the northwestern city of Petrozavodsk, Zharkova numerically replaces outgoing court president Vladimir Tumanov, who last October passed the upper age limit for judges of 70.
The court can play a key role in disputes between parliament and the president. Under the 1993 constitution, the president has huge powers but parliament can block government action.
Among issues the court may face soon is the fate of art treasures taken by the Red Army from Nazi Germany and other countries during World War Two.

Both houses of parliament voted down a Yeltsin veto on an opposition-sponsored bill that would effectively block any attempts by the president to return the hoard to Germany. Yeltsin has nonetheless refused to sign the bill into law.
The Federation Council on Tuesday sent it back to the Kremlin again, warning it would go to the Constitutional Court if Yeltsin continued to withhold his signature.
